Creation Ex Nihilo
kree-AY-shun eks NIH-hih-loh
n.
Latin ex nihilo, “out of nothing,” from ex (out of) + nihil (nothing). Creation ex nihilo is God’s bringing of all things into being from no preexisting matter.

📖 Biblical Definition

Creation ex nihilo is the doctrine that God, in the beginning, brought the entire universe into existence out of nothing—not fashioning it from preexisting matter, nor emanating it from His own substance, but calling it into being by the bare word of His power. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth”; He spake, and it was done; He commanded, and it stood fast. The writer to the Hebrews states the doctrine precisely: through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear. Before creation, God alone existed, eternal, self-sufficient, and triune; there was no matter, no space, no time, no co-eternal substance from which He shaped the world. By His sovereign will and almighty word He summoned all things from non-being into being, and pronounced them very good. This doctrine guards several vital truths. It establishes the Creator-creature distinction, the great divide between the eternal, independent God and the dependent, contingent creation. It refutes the dualism that posits eternal matter alongside God, the pantheism that makes the world an extension of the divine being, and the materialism that supposes the universe self-existent or eternal. It magnifies God’s sovereignty and freedom, for He created not from necessity but from the free counsel of His will, owing nothing to any. And it grounds His absolute lordship over all He has made: the world is His by right of creation, and to Him alone its worship is due, for He created all things, and for His pleasure they are and were created.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines CREATION as the act of creating; the act of causing to exist, and especially of bringing this world into existence; the production of a thing out of nothing.

expand to see more

CREATION, n. — 1. The act of creating; the act of causing to exist; and especially, the act of bringing this world into existence. 2. The act of making, by new combinations of matter, or of investing with a new character.

CREATE, v.t. — 1. To produce; to bring into being from nothing; to cause to exist. This is the proper and original sense of the word, applied to the work of God in the creation.

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 1:1 — "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth."

Hebrews 11:3 — "Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear."

Psalm 33:6 — "By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth."

Revelation 4:11 — "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Creation ex nihilo is denied by materialism (the universe is self-existent), by dualism (eternal matter alongside God), by pantheistic emanation (the world flows from God’s substance), and by every scheme that makes God a mere shaper of preexisting stuff.

expand to see more

The doctrine of creation out of nothing stands against a host of rival accounts of the world’s origin. Materialism, the reigning creed of secular science, holds the universe to be self-existent or eternal, requiring no Creator—matter and energy simply are, and from them all else arises by chance and law. Ancient and modern dualisms posit eternal matter existing alongside God, so that He is reduced from Creator to craftsman, a demiurge shaping stuff He did not make. Pantheistic and emanationist schemes have the world flow out of God’s own substance, blurring the Creator-creature distinction and making the cosmos a part or extension of the divine. Each of these denies the bare and glorious truth of Genesis: that God alone is eternal, and that He called all things from non-being by His word.

The stakes are high, for creation ex nihilo undergirds the whole of true religion. If matter is eternal or self-existent, God is not its absolute Lord, and the worship due Him as Maker is undermined. If the world emanates from His substance, then sin, decay, and death are somehow divine, and the Creator-creature line that grounds all worship and ethics is erased. The doctrine secures God’s sovereignty (He created freely, owing nothing), His lordship (the world is His by right of making), and the dependence of all things upon Him moment by moment. It also dignifies the material creation as the good work of a good God—neither an illusion to escape nor a divine fragment to worship, but a real world made from nothing, declared very good, and destined to be renewed.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The doctrine rests on the divine bārā’ (to create, used only of God’s work) accomplished by the dābār (word), framing worlds out of nihil (nothing).

Usage

"Creation ex nihilo means God called the universe from nothing by His word, not from preexisting matter."

"The doctrine refutes materialism, dualism, and pantheistic emanation alike, securing the Creator-creature distinction."

"Because God created all things ex nihilo, the world is His by right, and to Him alone its worship is due."
